name: Macro typing push

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-4, 2026-11-26): a food-ordering film pushes into a typed prompt at macro scale and glides along it behind a soft gradient caret.

technique: After text is typed in a UI, the camera pushes into it at macro scale and glides along the line with motion blur while a soft gradient caret leads the next letters, so a few typed words become a full-frame headline without a scene change.
purpose: Turn a typed query into the film's full-frame headline without a scene change.
visual_behaviour: Text typed in an input grows to macro scale as the camera pushes in, glides along the line with motion blur behind a soft gradient caret, then tilts away.
mechanics: Scale the input text 1 -> about 8x about the caret (0.2-0.3 s, power3.in); translate x along the line at constant speed with a directional smear of 6-12 px while letters type at 15-25 characters per second; caret = a 60-120 px gradient block (accent to transparent) with a solid 4 px edge; exit with a 3D tilt (rotateY 20-30 deg) and fade over 0.2-0.3 s.

decomposition.timing: Push 0.2-0.3 s; glide 0.7-1.0 s; exit 0.3 s (reference 2.12-3.15 s).

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: Final scale of the typed text

use_cases: Turning a typed query into the film's headline
failure_modes: A fast glide makes the blurred letters unreadable
Pixelated type if the text is rasterised before scaling

implementation.approach: Studio.type.typewriter at 15-25 characters/s; scale the text group from 1 to about 8x about the caret (0.2-0.3 s, power3.in); translate along the line at constant speed with Studio.fx.smear (6-12 px); caret = a gradient block with a solid 4 px edge; exit with rotateY 20-30 degrees and a fade. Keep the type as live text (not rasterised) so it stays sharp at 8x.

provenance.observed: The typed words 'spicy, crispy and filling' fill the frame at macro scale behind a blurred blue gradient caret and glide left with blur (2.12-2.79 s), then tilt away in 3D (2.88-3.15 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
